body_text: ¿Cuál es el mejor internet hogar en Colombia en 2026? Elegir el mejor internet para tu hogar en 2026 puede sonar complicado, pero no tiene por qué serlo. Hay muchísimas opciones —desde grandes operadores hasta proveedores locales— y es normal quedarte con la duda de qué plan te conviene. La verdad es que no hay una sola respuesta. El internet "ideal" depende de lo que necesitas, de dónde vives y del uso que le das a tu conexión. Con el teletrabajo, las clases virtuales y el streaming, hoy tener una conexión rápida y estable importa más que nunca. En esta guía te damos las herramientas para entender qué internet le sirve a tu hogar: comparamos los principales operadores y los factores que de verdad hacen la diferencia. La idea es que encuentres tu mejor opción para 2026, seas gamer, trabajes desde casa o simplemente quieras una conexión estable para toda la familia. Cuando entiendes el panorama, decides mejor: sin sorpresas, con un plan que se ajusta a tu presupuesto y a lo que esperas. Cómo hicimos esta comparativa: criterios y fuentes Para definir cuál es el mejor operador de internet hogar en Colombia usamos una metodología clara, con criterios objetivos y datos actualizados. No comparamos por suposiciones: comparamos con información real para que decidas con criterio. Estos son los criterios que evaluamos: Tecnología de conexión: priorizamos la fibra óptica por su estabilidad y velocidad. La fibra transmite datos con pulsos de luz por hilos de vidrio, así que no le afectan las interferencias eléctricas y mantiene la señal aunque la distancia sea larga —algo que el cobre no logra. Velocidad simétrica: miramos si la velocidad de subida es igual o cercana a la de bajada. Es clave para el teletrabajo, las clases virtuales y crear contenido. Hoy subes archivos pesados a la nube, haces videollamadas y te conectas a clases en línea: subir rápido pesa tanto como bajar rápido. Latencia: la tomamos en cuenta porque define las actividades que necesitan respuesta inmediata, como los videojuegos, las videollamadas sin cortes y las apps en la nube en tiempo real. Se mide en milisegundos (ms) y, mientras más baja, más fluida se siente la conexión. Cobertura: revisamos dónde está disponible cada servicio, ciudad por ciudad. La geografía de Colombia es diversa y complica el despliegue, así que la cobertura pesa mucho, sobre todo en zonas rurales o poco pobladas. Precios y planes: comparamos qué recibes por lo que pagas, con lupa en los costos ocultos, las promociones temporales y las cláusulas de permanencia. El plan más barato no siempre es el mejor si no cumple. Opiniones de usuarios y reportes de la SIC: escuchamos la experiencia real de los clientes y revisamos los informes de la Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) sobre calidad y atención. Esos reportes muestran, sin filtros, qué tan satisfecha está la gente y qué tan rápido resuelve cada operador. Consultamos fuentes oficiales de los operadores, reportes de la SIC y mediciones de velocidad de entidades reconocidas para darte una visión completa y confiable. Comparativa de operadores de internet para el hogar en Colombia Acá va el análisis de los principales operadores de internet hogar en Colombia, con sus fortalezas y sus debilidades, para que veas cuál te conviene. Somos Internet: fibra 100% simétrica en Antioquia y Bogotá En Somos ofrecemos fibra óptica 100% simétrica: subes tan rápido como bajas. Eso cambia el juego si trabajas desde casa, juegas o creas contenido, donde enviar datos pesa tanto como recibirlos. Nos enfocamos en una experiencia cercana, con planes transparentes y sin cláusulas de permanencia que te aten. Ventajas Desventajas fibra óptica 100% simétrica, baja latencia, atención cercana y planes sin permanencia, así te quedas con nosotros porque quieres, no porque te obliga un contrato. Nuestra propuesta es simple: calidad y transparencia. por ahora nuestra cobertura se concentra en Medellín (Valle de Aburrá), Rionegro y Bogotá , así que llegamos a menos zonas que los grandes operadores nacionales. Claro: la mayor cobertura del país Claro es uno de los operadores con más presencia en Colombia y llega a un montón de ciudades y municipios. Su red HFC (Híbrido de Fibra Coaxial) le permite estar en muchos lugares, y ya está ampliando su red de fibra óptica. Sus paquetes que juntan internet, telefonía móvil y televisión suelen atraer a quien quiere todo con un solo proveedor. Ventajas Desventajas cobertura amplia, variedad de planes y paquetes con televisión y telefonía. Su red HFC llega a zonas donde la fibra todavía no. la velocidad de subida suele ser menor que la de bajada (asimetría), y eso golpea a quien sube muchos archivos, vive en videollamadas o transmite en vivo. Además, la calidad cambia según tengas HFC o fibra. Movistar: líder en velocidad promedio Movistar es un competidor fuerte en internet hogar, sobre todo por su fibra óptica. Invirtió mucho en esta tecnología, así que ofrece velocidades altas y estables, con buena presencia en las principales ciudades. Su apuesta por la fibra directa al hogar (FTTH) le ayuda a dar una experiencia sólida en velocidad y estabilidad. Ventajas Desventajas alta velocidad de descarga, buena estabilidad en fibra, planes competitivos y una apuesta creciente por la simetría. Suele destacar en las mediciones de velocidad de terceros. su cobertura de fibra crece, pero todavía no llega tan lejos como la de Claro, así que puede faltar en zonas menos urbanas. Tigo (UNE): precio competitivo, simetría limitada Tigo —antes UNE en algunas regiones— ofrece planes de internet hogar a precios competitivos. Combina HFC y fibra óptica según la zona, y suele apostar por paquetes que juntan internet, televisión y telefonía para captar a quien mira el precio. Ventajas Desventajas precios atractivos, buenos paquetes y presencia consolidada en varias regiones, sobre todo en Antioquia y el Eje Cafetero. la simetría en sus planes HFC es limitada y la calidad cambia bastante según la zona y la red disponible. Su fibra sigue en expansión. ETB: la latencia más baja, solo en Bogotá ETB es fuerte en Bogotá, donde se ganó buena fama por su fibra óptica. Se destaca por una de las latencias más bajas del mercado, ideal para quien exige respuesta inmediata: gamers, desarrolladores o gente que vive de apps en la nube. Al ser empresa de servicios públicos, cuida mucho su infraestructura. Ventajas Desventajas latencia muy baja, alta velocidad y estabilidad en fibra. Una opción premium para quien vive en la capital, con un servicio al cliente bien valorado en su zona. su cobertura se concentra en Bogotá y alrededores, así que queda corta para el resto del país. Qué evaluar antes de contratar internet hogar Antes de decidirse por el mejor internet hogar en Colombia, es fundamental que evalúe algunos aspectos clave que impactarán directamente su experiencia. No se trata solo de la velocidad, sino de la calidad general del servicio y cómo se adapta a su estilo de vida digital. Fibra óptica vs. HFC: por qué importa la tecnología La tecnología de conexión es uno de los factores más importantes. La fibra óptica es, hoy, la mejor opción. Transmite datos a la velocidad de la luz por hilos de vidrio, y eso te da: Más velocidad: planes de cientos o hasta miles de megas, muy por encima de otras tecnologías. Más estabilidad: le afectan menos las interferencias eléctricas, el clima o la distancia, así que la conexión se mantiene pareja. Menos latencia: clave para todo lo que pasa en tiempo real, porque los datos viajan más directo. Lista para el futuro: la fibra aguanta la demanda de datos que viene, así que es una inversión a largo plazo para tu casa. El HFC (Híbrido de Fibra Coaxial), en cambio, mezcla fibra con cable coaxial. Es una tecnología sólida y muy extendida, pero suele tener más latencia y menos velocidad de subida que la fibra pura, por cómo funciona el cable coaxial y porque la red se comparte. Velocidad simétrica: la métrica que casi nadie compara Cuando piensas en velocidad de internet, seguramente piensas solo en la descarga (bajada). Pero la velocidad simétrica pesa igual, sobre todo hoy: significa que subes a la misma velocidad —o casi— con la que bajas. ¿Por qué importa? Teletrabajo: subes archivos pesados sin esperas, haces videollamadas en HD sin cortes y usas plataformas en la nube con fluidez. Gaming: tus datos llegan al servidor sin retraso, así bajas el "lag" y juegas mejor en línea. Creación de contenido: subes videos a YouTube, transmites en vivo en Twitch o Facebook Live sin cortes y compartes proyectos pesados sin sufrir. Copias de seguridad en la nube: sincronizas tus archivos rápido y sin dramas, así tu información siempre queda respaldada. Educación virtual: estudiantes y profesores interactúan sin trabas, suben tareas y participan en clase en tiempo real. Muchos operadores venden bajadas altísimas pero subidas mucho más bajas (por ejemplo, 500 Mbps de bajada y solo 50 de subida). Si estas actividades son parte de tu día a día, busca fibra óptica 100% simétrica para una experiencia de verdad equilibrada. Latencia: clave para gaming, videollamadas y teletrabajo La latencia es el tiempo que tarda un dato en ir de tu dispositivo al servidor y volver. Se mide en milisegundos (ms): mientras más baja, más rápido responde todo. Gaming: una latencia alta se traduce en "lag", y ahí tus acciones en pantalla no responden a tiempo. Por debajo de 20-30 ms es lo ideal para juego competitivo. Videollamadas: con latencia alta las conversaciones se cortan, se escuchan con eco o se desincronizan. Teletrabajo: afecta las apps en la nube, la colaboración en documentos y la comunicación con tus colegas. Resultado: frustración y menos productividad. Aplicaciones críticas: en lo profesional, la baja latencia es clave para cosas que exigen respuesta inmediata, como el trading o el control remoto de maquinaria. Si eres gamer, vives en videollamadas o dependes de la nube para trabajar, prioriza operadores con baja latencia, como los de fibra óptica directa al hogar (FTTH): esa tecnología reduce la congestión y acorta la distancia que recorren los datos. Atención al cliente y quejas ante la SIC La calidad no termina en la velocidad. La atención al cliente también pesa —y mucho—. ¿Qué tan fácil es contactar al operador cuando tienes un problema? ¿Te resuelven rápido y de verdad? Un buen soporte marca la diferencia entre pasar un mal rato o salir de la falla en minutos. Puedes consultar los reportes de la Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) para ver cuántas quejas recibe cada operador y qué tan rápido las resuelve. Esos informes, disponibles en la web de la SIC, te dan una idea real de la satisfacción de los usuarios y de cómo responde cada empresa ante problemas comunes: cortes, facturación mal hecha o promesas que no se cumplen. Un buen servicio, con varios canales (teléfono, chat, redes) y tiempos de respuesta cortos, cambia por completo la experiencia. El mejor internet hogar según tu ciudad La disponibilidad y la calidad del internet cambian bastante de una ciudad a otra. Lo que es la mejor opción en una región puede no serlo en otra, porque cambian la infraestructura, la inversión de los operadores y hasta la topografía. Mejor internet en Medellín y Antioquia Si buscas el mejor internet en Medellín y Antioquia , tienes de dónde escoger. Claro y Tigo tienen buena presencia, con redes HFC y fibra en expansión. Pero si lo tuyo es la fibra óptica 100% simétrica y una atención cercana y de verdad, Somos es una gran alternativa. Llegamos con el internet más rápido de Rionegro , internet para apartamentos en Sabaneta e internet en Caldas, Antioquia , con planes pensados para hogares —y también para empresas grandes, medianas y pequeñas— porque la región cada vez pide más conectividad de calidad. Mejor internet en Bogotá En Bogotá la competencia es dura: es la capital y el centro económico del país. ETB pega fuerte con su fibra de baja latencia, y es la favorita de muchos bogotanos. Movistar también tiene una excelente red de fibra, con alta velocidad y estabilidad. Y si buscas el mejor internet para tu hogar en Bogotá con foco en simetría, planes transparentes y una atención distinta, Somos es una opción que vale la pena mirar: llegamos a la capital para hacer las cosas diferente. Qué dicen los usuarios reales en 2026 Las opiniones de los usuarios son un termómetro clave para medir la calidad real de un servicio, más allá de los datos técnicos. En 2026, los foros, las redes, las plataformas de reseñas y los grupos de consumidores están llenos de comentarios sobre los operadores de internet en Colombia. Vale la pena leer reseñas recientes, porque la calidad y las ofertas cambian rápido. Mucha gente valora la estabilidad de la conexión, la velocidad simétrica para el teletrabajo y el entretenimiento, y un soporte que responde. Las quejas suelen ir por el mismo lado: atención al cliente floja, intermitencias inesperadas, velocidades que no llegan a lo prometido (sobre todo en horas pico o en tecnologías que no son fibra pura) y procesos enredados para resolver problemas o cancelar. Leer la experiencia de otros te da una idea más clara de qué esperar y te ahorra malos ratos. Preguntas frecuentes sobre internet hogar en Colombia Acá respondemos las dudas más comunes cuando buscas el mejor internet hogar en Colombia. ¿Cuántos megas necesito para mi hogar? Depende de cuántas personas viven en tu casa, cuántos dispositivos conectan y qué hacen con ellos. Mira tanto la velocidad de bajada como la de subida. 1-2 personas (uso básico): 50-100 Mbps. Alcanza para navegar, redes sociales, streaming en HD en uno o dos dispositivos y correo. 3-4 personas (uso moderado): 100-300 Mbps. Ideal para streaming 4K, teletrabajo liviano, gaming de vez en cuando, videollamadas y varios dispositivos a la vez. 5+ personas o uso intensivo: 300 Mbps o más. Para hogares con muchos dispositivos inteligentes, teletrabajo pesado, gaming competitivo, varios televisores en 4K al tiempo y creación de contenido. Recuerda que la velocidad de subida importa si haces videollamadas, subes archivos grandes a la nube o transmites en vivo. Un consejo: contrata un poco más de lo que crees que necesitas y te ahorras cuellos de botella más adelante. ¿Cuál es el internet más rápido de Colombia? Hoy, el internet más rápido suele venir de operadores con fibra óptica que invirtieron fuerte en su red. Movistar y ETB (en Bogotá) destacan por sus altas velocidades de bajada, a menudo por encima de 500 Mbps y hasta 1 Gbps en sus planes premium. Pero si hablamos de velocidad simétrica, en Somos ofrecemos planes donde subes tan rápido como bajas con planes de hasta 2,000 megas , y eso se siente en el día a día para todo lo que necesita datos en las dos vías. Las mediciones de entidades como Ookla (Speedtest) o la propia SIC suelen confirmar estas tendencias, aunque los resultados cambian según la zona y la hora. ¿Qué es mejor: fibra óptica, HFC o internet 5G para el hogar? Depende de lo que necesitas y de lo que haya disponible en tu zona: Fibra óptica: la mejor opción. Te da las mayores velocidades (hasta 10 Gbps o más), la menor latencia y la mayor estabilidad, porque no le afectan las interferencias eléctricas. Sirve para cualquier usuario, y brilla con gamers y teletrabajadores. HFC (Híbrido de Fibra Coaxial): una buena salida si la fibra no llega a tu zona. Da velocidades decentes, pero con más latencia y menos subida que la fibra pura. Es una tecnología madura y muy extendida en las ciudades. Internet 5G para el hogar: una alternativa inalámbrica que usa la red móvil 5G a través de un router. Funciona bien donde no hay fibra ni HFC, con velocidades altas e instalación rápida. Eso sí, su rendimiento cambia según la cobertura 5G, la congestión de la red y la distancia a la antena. Y ojo: algunos planes ponen límites de datos o políticas de uso justo que afectan a quien consume mucho. Internet satelital: no estaba en el borrador, pero vale mencionarlo. Es la opción para zonas rurales o muy remotas donde no llega nada más. Cubre casi cualquier lugar, pero suele traer velocidades más bajas, latencia muy alta (por la distancia a los satélites) y costos más altos. Para la mayoría de hogares urbanos y suburbanos, la fibra óptica sigue siendo la mejor por rendimiento y confiabilidad. ¿Puedo cancelar mi plan si el servicio es malo? Sí. Puedes cancelar si el servicio no cumple con lo que contrataste o si tiene fallas repetidas que el operador no resuelve en un tiempo razonable. La Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) es la entidad que protege tus derechos como consumidor en Colombia. Revisa las cláusulas de permanencia de tu contrato, porque algunos operadores cobran penalidades si cancelas antes de tiempo sin una causa justificada. Pero si la falla es del operador y puedes demostrarlo (con reportes de fallas o mediciones por debajo de lo prometido), esas penalidades no deberían aplicarse. Además, la ley colombiana contempla el "derecho de retracto": puedes desistir del contrato dentro de los primeros cinco días hábiles, sin ninguna penalidad. Guarda siempre tus comunicaciones con el operador y, si no te resuelven, presenta una queja formal ante la SIC. Somos es, dentro de los operadores grandes, el único que no pone fricciones en la salida y ofrece instalación gratis sin contratos vinculantes. Conclusión: así eliges el mejor internet para tu hogar Elegir el mejor internet hogar en Colombia en 2026 empieza por mirar lo que de verdad necesitas, sin dejarte llevar solo por el precio o por la velocidad de bajada. Ten en cuenta la tecnología (prioriza la fibra óptica por su estabilidad y velocidad), la velocidad simétrica (clave para teletrabajo y creación de contenido), la latencia (fundamental para gaming y videollamadas) y la atención al cliente (para no vivir un via crucis cuando algo falle). Si vives en Medellín, Antioquia o Bogotá y quieres fibra óptica 100% simétrica con un servicio cercano y transparente, en Somos vale la pena que nos mires. Para otras regiones, compara con calma las ofertas de Claro, Movistar y Tigo, siempre atento a los detalles del plan, a la tecnología disponible en tu zona y a lo que dicen otros usuarios. Al final, el mejor internet es el que mejor te sirve a ti, a tu presupuesto y a lo que tu hogar necesita todos los días.

title: How to Improve SAT Score by 200 Points: 5-Step 2026 Plan
summary: Learn how to improve SAT score by 200 points with a 5-step plan, timelines, and error logs. Diagnose gaps and start your 2026 study plan now.
body_text: How to Improve SAT Score by 200 Points: 5-Step 2026 Plan TLDR A 200-point SAT increase is realistic for many students, especially those starting below 1300 who have clear content gaps in math or grammar. It does not come from taking practice tests on repeat. The proven path is to take a diagnostic, identify the specific domains costing you points, drill those skills with focused practice, keep an error log, and retest every one to two weeks. Most students need 8 to 12 weeks of consistent work, though shorter timelines can work for students with obvious, fixable gaps. A 200-point SAT improvement means raising your total score by 200 points on the 400 to 1600 scale. Going from 1100 to 1300, or from 1280 to 1480. That kind of jump is far beyond normal test-day variation, which College Board puts at roughly plus or minus 40 points on the total score. So a 200-point gain is not luck. It is the result of structured work. The good news: it happens. A 2017 College Board and Khan Academy study found that more than 16,000 students gained 200 or more points through personalized official practice. Twenty hours of focused practice was associated with a 115-point average increase . Some students report gains in the 90 to 200 point range from SAT practice alone. The catch: how to improve your SAT score by 200 points depends almost entirely on where you start, what is actually costing you points, and whether you study the right things. If you want a structured starting point, take a free diagnostic to see where your score stands right now. Quick Answer: How Can You Improve Your SAT Score by 200 Points? A 200-point SAT increase is achievable for many students, especially those scoring below 1300. The fastest improvements come from identifying weak content areas instead of repeatedly taking practice tests. Most students need 8–12 weeks of focused study, regular full-length Digital SAT practice tests, an error log, and targeted review of Math and Standard English Conventions. Students already scoring above 1400 usually see slower gains because they must eliminate small mistakes rather than learn new concepts. Key Takeaways Goal Recommendation Raise score by 200 points Plan for 8–12 weeks Best place to gain points Algebra + Grammar Biggest mistake Taking practice tests without reviewing mistakes Best study tool Official Bluebook practice tests Full-length tests Every 1–2 weeks Daily study 45–90 minutes Track progress Maintain an error log What Does a 200-Point SAT Increase Actually Mean? The SAT total score is the sum of two section scores. Reading and Writing ranges from 200 to 800, and Math ranges from 200 to 800, giving a total range of 400 to 1600 . A 200-point total increase usually comes from gains across both sections. Maybe +120 in Math and +80 in Reading and Writing. Maybe +100 in each. The split depends on where your weaknesses are. The digital SAT is 2 hours and 14 minutes long. It includes 54 Reading and Writing questions and 44 Math questions, split into two modules per section. The second module adjusts in difficulty based on how you performed in the first. This adaptive structure matters for prep because doing well on Module 1 gives you access to harder (and higher-scoring) questions in Module 2. Here is a quick way to think about what a 200-point gain looks like at different starting points: Current Score Target Score What It Means 900 1100 Building core SAT skills and test stamina 1050 1250 Fixing major math and grammar gaps 1200 1400 Adding hard-question accuracy and error review 1300 1500 Precision work and fewer careless mistakes 1400 1600 Extremely difficult, near-perfect performance required The mean SAT score for the class of 2025 was 1029 , with mean section scores of 521 in Reading and Writing and 508 in Math. Only 39% of test takers met both college readiness benchmarks. For most students scoring around or below the mean, a 200-point improvement is within reach with the right approach. Is a 200-Point SAT Increase Realistic? Yes, but the difficulty varies enormously by starting score. Below 1200: This is where the biggest gains happen fastest. Students at this level often have broad content gaps, things like forgotten algebra rules, shaky grammar foundations, or unfamiliarity with the test format. Filling those gaps can produce dramatic score jumps because each fixed gap eliminates multiple missed questions. 1200 to 1350: Still very realistic. The work shifts from “learning basics” to “targeted practice plus timing.” Students in this range usually know most of the content but make mistakes under pressure, misread questions, or run out of time on harder modules. 1350 to 1450: This is where improving your SAT score by 200 points gets genuinely hard. You are no longer fixing content gaps. You are eliminating careless errors, mastering the hardest question types, and performing at near-ceiling accuracy on easy and medium questions. Practitioners on Reddit note that gains become significantly harder above the 1400s, and CollegeConfidential users make the same observation about the difference between reaching 1390 and reaching 1540. 1450 and above: A full 200-point increase may be mathematically impossible because the SAT caps at 1600. At this level, target section-specific marginal gains instead. One student shared on LinkedIn about going from 1350 to 1550 in roughly 50 days. Their approach: focused topic practice, flashcards, not burning through all practice tests too quickly, starting vocabulary work 2 to 3 months early, and avoiding multi-day study gaps. That lines up with what works at higher baselines, where consistency and precision matter more than volume. How Much Can Your SAT Score Improve Based on Your Starting Score? One of the biggest factors affecting improvement is your starting score. Students with lower scores usually improve faster because they have more foundational concepts to learn, while high-scoring students must eliminate increasingly smaller mistakes. Starting Score Typical Improvement Potential Difficulty Below 1000 200–400 points Moderate 1000–1150 150–300 points Moderate 1150–1300 150–250 points Moderate 1300–1450 80–200 points Difficult Above 1450 20–120 points Very Difficult How Long Does It Take to Raise Your SAT Score by 200 Points? There is no universal answer, but there are realistic ranges. Timeline What to Expect 1 week Possible small gain. A 200-point jump is unlikely unless your baseline was artificially low. 10 days Ambitious. PrepScholar’s cram plan compresses about 54 hours into 10 days and calls it ambitious . Not ideal if you have more time. 4 to 6 weeks Possible for students with clear math and grammar gaps who can practice daily. 8 to 12 weeks The best practical window for a 200-point goal. Enough time for diagnosis, content review, error correction, and multiple practice tests. 3+ months Strongest window for durable improvement, especially for Reading and Writing gains and high-score targets. The College Board and Khan Academy data showed that 20 hours of personalized practice was associated with a 115-point average increase, but that is an average across a large study, not an individual guarantee. Community examples on Reddit range from 50 to 150 hours for major gains. The variation makes sense: a student closing basic algebra gaps needs fewer hours than someone trying to master hard Module 2 questions. A score predictor can help you estimate whether your current pace is on track for your target score. Why Students Fail to Improve Their SAT Scores Many students study for months without seeing meaningful improvement because they spend time on activities that feel productive instead of fixing the actual reasons they lose points. Common causes include: Taking practice tests without reviewing mistakes Using random worksheets instead of targeted practice Ignoring weak subject areas Memorizing answers instead of learning concepts Never practicing under timed conditions Studying inconsistently Skipping official Digital SAT practice tests Not learning how adaptive modules affect scoring Research consistently shows that feedback and deliberate practice outperform repetitive testing alone. The 5-Step Plan to Improve Your SAT Score by 200 Points Step 1: Take a Full-Length Digital Diagnostic Before you study anything, you need to know what is actually costing you points. Take a full-length, timed digital SAT practice test using Bluebook or a realistic simulation that matches the digital format. Record everything: Total score, Reading and Writing score, Math score Domain-level performance (which content areas were strongest and weakest) Pacing notes (did you run out of time?) Easy questions you got wrong versus hard questions you got wrong College Board recommends full-length practice tests to understand strengths, weak areas, and test-day pacing. The easy misses matter most. Getting a hard question wrong is expected. Getting an easy question wrong means there is a fixable gap, and that is where points come from fastest. Step 2: Build a Point Map Now figure out where 200 points will actually come from. The SAT tests eight content domains. Four in Reading and Writing: Information and Ideas, Craft and Structure, Expression of Ideas, and Standard English Conventions. Four in Math: Algebra, Advanced Math, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, and Geometry and Trigonometry . Look at your diagnostic results by domain. Where did you miss the most questions? That is your point source map. Current Score Target Main Source of Points 1050 1250 Math basics + grammar rules + timing 1180 1380 Algebra/Advanced Math + Standard English Conventions + practice test review 1280 1480 Harder Module 2 math + evidence questions + careless mistake reduction 1380 1580 Extremely hard; needs near-perfect execution across all domains Step 3: Fix Content Gaps Before Taking More Tests This is where most students go wrong. They take another practice test before they have actually learned anything new. A tutor-like reply in one of the top Reddit threads on this topic puts it bluntly: simply taking practice tests over and over trains you to keep getting the same score . Think of it as “practice test debt.” Every unreviewed miss becomes a repeated miss. If you miss systems of equations every time, another full-length test will not fix systems of equations. You need a focused lesson, then a set of similar questions, then a delayed redo of those questions a few days later. This approach is backed by learning science. A major review of study techniques rated practice testing and distributed practice (spacing out study sessions) as high-utility techniques that work across ages and learning conditions. Work through targeted SAT problem sets organized by domain and difficulty to close gaps efficiently. Step 4: Keep an Error Log An error log is the difference between “studying a lot” and “studying the right thing.” Every time you miss a question, write down why. Question Section Domain Why I Missed It Correct Concept Faster Method Redo Date Categorize your misses. Not all wrong answers are the same: Content gap: You did not know the rule or formula. Setup error: You knew the concept but set up the problem wrong. Misread: You answered a different question than what was asked. Timing error: You could solve it untimed but not under pressure. Tool error: Desmos, annotation, or answer elimination would have helped. Careless mistake: Your process was correct but execution was sloppy. Strategy error: You chose a slow path when a faster method existed. Reddit users in recent threads explicitly recommend this kind of categorization. One commenter described sorting errors by concept gap, careless error, timing issue, misreading, and strategy problem as a turning point in their prep. This mirrors what College Board’s My Practice review and domain reports are designed to help with. Step 5: Retest, but Not Too Often Full-length practice tests are checkpoints, not the workout itself. Here is a reasonable cadence: 8 to 12 week plan: Full practice test every 2 weeks 4 to 6 week plan: Full practice test every 1 to 2 weeks Last 10 days: One full test early, targeted review after, no exhausting marathon the day before College Board recommends taking a full-length practice test about two weeks before test day and reviewing every question and explanation afterward. The goal is to confirm that your targeted practice is working and to identify any remaining weak spots. A practitioner on LinkedIn made a useful observation: digital SAT prep often breaks down after practice tests because students see their score but do not know what to fix next. The fix is turning every mock test into an action plan, not just a number. Which SAT Section Is Easiest to Improve? Not every SAT section offers the same opportunity for improvement. SAT Area Difficulty to Improve Typical Speed Algebra Easy Fast Grammar Easy Fast Problem Solving & Data Analysis Medium Moderate Geometry & Trigonometry Medium Moderate Reading Comprehension Hard Slower Vocabulary in Context Hard Slow What Should You Study First for the Fastest 200 Points? Not all SAT content is equally improvable. Prioritize the areas where gains come fastest. 1. Math content gaps. If you are missing questions in Algebra, Advanced Math, or Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, these are often the fastest points available. Math rules are concrete, and once you learn them, they stick. Practitioners on Reddit repeatedly identify math as the quickest path to points, especially for students around the 1100 to 1200 range. 2. Standard English Conventions. Grammar and punctuation rules are learnable and repeatable. Sentence boundaries, subject-verb agreement, modifier placement, punctuation. These show up in a defined portion of every Reading and Writing section. Drilling them is high return. 3. Transitions and rhetorical synthesis. The Expression of Ideas domain tests revision, transitions, and rhetorical goals. These question types follow predictable patterns and respond well to targeted practice. 4. Desmos and digital tools. College Board tells students to learn the built-in Desmos calculator and practice with it. Reddit users describe Desmos mastery as a quick math-score lever, though higher-score commenters warn that hard Module 2 questions still require flexible algebra and concept knowledge. Learn Desmos because it is a real test-day tool, but do not use it as a substitute for understanding the math. 5. Vocabulary and reading stamina. College Board’s Craft and Structure domain includes high-utility words and phrases in context. A self-described SAT tutor on Reddit advises students below 650 to 700 in Reading and Writing to read more, study vocabulary, and use spaced repetition. This is the slowest area to improve, which is why starting early matters. For daily SAT practice by domain , focus on the areas your error log flags most often. Sample 8-Week SAT Study Plan for a 200-Point Increase This schedule assumes 45 to 90 minutes of practice most days. Adjust based on your starting score and available time. Week Focus 1 Diagnostic test. Build error log. Identify your top 3 weak domains. 2 Math gap #1 + grammar gap #1. Daily 30 to 60 minute drills. 3 Math gap #2 + Reading and Writing evidence questions. Timed mini sets. 4 Full practice test. 2-hour review session. Update your point map. 5 Harder math topics + Desmos workflows + Standard English Conventions. 6 Reading and Writing weak domains + timed modules. Redo old misses from error log. 7 Full practice test. Simulate test-morning routine. Patch remaining errors. 8 Light review. Redo error log highlights. Lock in sleep schedule. Final pacing plan. Compressed 4-Week Plan Week Focus 1 Diagnostic + content triage. Identify biggest gaps. 2 Daily targeted practice. Math and grammar priority. 3 Full test + deep review. Hard-question and pacing practice. 4 Final test early in the week. Redo misses. Light review before test day. 10-Day Emergency Plan Use this only if you have no other option. Even PrepScholar, which publishes a 10-day cram plan, frames it as ambitious. Day 1: Full diagnostic Days 2 to 4: Biggest math and grammar gaps Day 5: Timed modules Day 6: Second full test Days 7 to 8: Review errors and redo missed question types Day 9: Light mixed practice, no marathon Day 10: Rest and test logistics Common Mistakes That Keep Students from Improving Taking practice tests without reviewing them. This is the single most common mistake. One Reddit commenter described it perfectly: repeating practice tests without analyzing mistakes just trains you to get the same score. Every test you take without deep review is wasted. Studying what feels comfortable. It is tempting to spend time on topics you already know because it feels productive. The top-ranking Reddit thread on this topic warns against wasting time reviewing already-strong areas. Your error log should dictate what you study, not your comfort level. Ignoring the digital format. The SAT is now adaptive by module. Students can move within a module, but once it ends, the next begins. If your prep does not include the digital tools (Desmos, annotation, mark-for-review, answer eliminator), you are leaving points on the table. One practitioner on LinkedIn argues that understanding the adaptive test mechanics matters more than brute-force volume. Using low-fidelity practice questions. An SAT tutor reviewing third-party digital SAT practice materials on LinkedIn noted that many are not very accurate compared to official questions. Official College Board materials should be your benchmark. Third-party tools can add volume and explanations, but watch for question styles that do not match the real test. Not sleeping enough. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine recommends that teenagers get 8 to 10 hours of sleep per night. Test-day exhaustion can erase weeks of gains. This applies to practice sessions too. Studying tired is practicing being tired. Do You Need a Tutor or Prep Tool? Not always. A tutor on Reddit’s r/digitalSATs advises that many students can self-study effectively with official materials, the right direction, and sufficient practice. The key phrase is “the right direction.” Self-study works when you can diagnose your own mistakes. A tutor, AI tutor, or structured prep platform becomes more valuable when: You cannot figure out why you are missing questions Your score has plateaued after 2 to 3 full practice tests You keep repeating the same error types Your target is high (for example, 1400 to 1550) Your test date is close and you need help prioritizing An AI tutor can fill the gap between official materials and expensive private tutoring by providing instant explanations and guided practice on demand. The important thing is that whatever tool you use, it should help you identify and fix weaknesses, not just generate more practice volume. Start with a free SAT diagnostic to see exactly where your points are hiding. How to Know If Your Study Plan Is Working A study plan should produce measurable progress over time. Rather than focusing only on total SAT score, monitor several indicators each week. Metric Healthy Progress Accuracy Increasing Time per question Decreasing Repeated mistakes Declining Easy-question accuracy Above 90% Practice test scores Trending upward If these metrics remain unchanged after two or three weeks, adjust your study plan rather than simply increasing study hours. Frequently Asked Questions Can I improve my SAT score by 200 points in a month? Possible, but ambitious. It is more realistic if you are starting below 1200 and have obvious math or grammar gaps that can be fixed quickly. Students starting above 1300 will find a one-month timeline much harder for a full 200-point gain. Can I improve by 200 points in one week? Technically possible but very unlikely. A week is enough to learn test format, fix a few obvious content gaps, and reduce test anxiety. But 200 points in seven days requires everything to go right, and that is not a plan you should count on. How many hours does a 200-point SAT increase take? There is no guaranteed number. The College Board and Khan Academy study found 20 hours was associated with a 115-point average increase, while 6 to 8 hours was associated with 90 points. Anecdotal examples on Reddit range from 50 to over 150 hours for large gains. The quality of those hours matters more than the quantity. Is math easier to improve than Reading and Writing? For most students, yes. Math content gaps are easier to isolate and drill because the rules are concrete. If you cannot solve systems of equations, you learn systems of equations and then you can. Reading and Writing improvement, especially vocabulary and passage comprehension, tends to build more slowly because it depends on broader skills like reading fluency and contextual reasoning. Should I use only official SAT practice materials? Official materials should be your benchmark because College Board writes the SAT, and Bluebook practice tests simulate the real digital format. Third-party tools can help with additional volume and explanations, but always verify that the question style matches the actual test. Browse additional SAT resources that complement official practice. Do I need a tutor to improve by 200 points? Not necessarily. Official resources, a strong error log, and consistent targeted practice may be enough. A tutor or AI tutor is most useful when you cannot identify why you are missing questions, when your score has plateaued, or when you have a short timeline and need someone to prioritize your study plan. Is a 200-point SAT improvement guaranteed? No. Anyone who guarantees a specific point increase is overpromising. What the data shows is that structured, focused practice consistently produces score gains, and that 200-point improvements are common enough (over 16,000 students achieved it in one study) to be a realistic goal for many students. But individual results depend on starting score, study consistency, content gaps, and time invested. What if my score stops improving? A plateau usually means one of three things: you are studying the wrong topics, you are not reviewing mistakes deeply enough, or you are at a score level where gains require precision rather than volume. Revisit your error log, shift to harder question types, or consider whether switching to a different format might help. Some students find that trying ACT practice reveals a better fit for their strengths.

title: Ethos Signs Erin Andrews as Its Next Sports Partner in Growing Campaign to Make Life Insurance Accessible for Every Family
summary: Ethos Signs Erin Andrews as Its Next Sports Partner in Growing Campaign to Make Life Insurance Accessible for Every Family ...
body_text: AUSTIN, Texas, Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ethos (NASDAQ: LIFE), a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to democratize access to life insurance, today announced that it has signed its next sports partner, Erin Andrews, Fox Sports NFL reporter, co-host of 99 To Beat, entrepreneur, and cervical cancer survivor. Andrews will serve as a national ambassador for Ethos in an upcoming campaign, details of which will be announced at a later date. “I've spent my career around athletes who prepare obsessively for every possible outcome on the field,” said Erin Andrews. “But when it comes to protecting their families financially, so many people, athletes and fans alike, just haven't gotten around to it. I've been through enough in my own life to know that you can't wait for the perfect moment. I'm proud to be joining the Ethos family, and I can't wait to share more.” The signing marks the latest chapter in Ethos' deepening relationship with the world of sports. Earlier this year, the company launched a campaign with baseball Hall of Famer David Ortiz, whose own near-death experience and profound personal losses gave powerful authenticity to the message that no family should be left without a plan. In late 2025, Ethos partnered with NFL legend and broadcaster Boomer Esiason, who has spoken openly about losing his mother at age seven—a tragedy made harder by the absence of life insurance. These three sports figures have stories that couldn't be more different. But a common thread runs through them: each has lived through enough to know that preparation and protection aren't abstract concepts — they define what happens to the people you love most. Erin Andrews brings a different and complementary dimension to that story. Having navigated serious personal health challenges in the public eye, Andrews speaks to audiences that previous Ethos partners have not always reached, particularly women and younger families who are among the most underserved demographics when it comes to life insurance coverage. “Erin Andrews is someone who commands trust and authentic connection across an enormous and diverse audience,” said Prassath Leelakrishnan, Chief Growth Officer at Ethos. “She speaks to fans, to families, to women who are thinking about their futures. And she brings genuine conviction to this partnership. Together with Boomer and David, she completes a remarkable group of sports voices who each carry a personal understanding of why this matters. We look forward to sharing more about what we're building together.” The signing reflects Ethos' broader strategic vision: to build a roster of trusted sports voices who each speak authentically to a different corner of the American family. Ethos is working to ensure that no matter who you are or where you encounter the brand, you find a face and a story that feels like yours. For more information about Ethos, visit www.ethos.com . About Ethos Ethos is a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to protect families by democratizing access to life insurance and empowering agents at scale. With its robust three-sided technology platform, Ethos is transforming the life insurance experience for consumers, agents, and carriers alike. Ethos offers instant, accessible products and a seamless online process that requires no medical exams and just a few health questions; it eliminates traditional barriers, making it easier than ever for everyone to protect their families. Through its platform, Ethos is redefining how life insurance is bought, sold, and underwritten. Learn more at ethos.com . About Erin Andrews Entrepreneur and broadcaster Erin Andrews is most widely known for her work as a member of FOX Sports’ A Team, reporting on “FOX NFL Sunday.” She can also be seen as co-host of the FOX game show, 99 To Beat, alongside Ken Jeong, with Season 2 releasing September 2026. Andrews garnered notable attention as an entrepreneur, launching WEAR by Erin Andrews in October 2019. The clothing and accessories brand, worn by the likes of Kelly Clarkson and Taylor Swift, focuses on fashion first licensed team apparel for women to wear on gameday and beyond, and has quickly become one of the top selling female licensed brands. In addition to being a trailblazer in the sports world, Andrews co-hosts the popular iHeartRadio podcast “Calm Down with Erin and Charissa,” which features unfiltered conversations between two girlfriends about life, sports, and pretty much every random topic that needs to be dissected. For 11 seasons, Andrews co-hosted ABC’s long-running reality series “Dancing with the Stars,” alongside Tom Bergeron. Recent notable appearances include her coverage of Super Bowl LIV, Super Bowl LI, Super Bowl XLVIII, the 2021 NFC Championship Game, the 2015 & 2014 World Series, the 2015 & 2014 MLB All Star Games and hosting FOX’s “Prime Time College Football Pregame Show.” Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. title: Highlighting its Commitment to Educating Servicemembers and their Extended Families, AMU Becomes National Sponsor of Our Community Salutes (OCS)
summary: Highlighting its Commitment to Educating Servicemembers and their Extended Families, AMU Becomes National Sponsor of Our Community Salutes (OCS)
body_text: Charles Town, WV – May 18, 2026 – Affirming its ongoing support of active-duty students, American Military University (AMU) is now a National Sponsor for Our Community Salutes, USA (OCS), a national 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting future enlisted service members and their families as they start their military journey. “AMU is committed to empowering servicemembers as they grow in their careers and personal lives,” said Tonda Navarrette, Vice President of Military Outreach for AMU. “As our country approaches its historic 250th birthday, AMU is proud to stand alongside Our Community Salutes in uplifting the next generation of servicemembers, and their extended families.” Since its founding in 2009, OCS has hosted recognition ceremonies in cities around the country honoring high-school seniors who plan to enlist into the military immediately after high-school graduation. OCS also provides developmental programs, guidance, resources, and community support to new enlistees, and their families, as they transition into military service. “Our Community Salutes offers a meaningful way to honor our country’s servicemembers as they take their oath to help defend our country,” said Dr. Kenneth E. Hartman, Founder and President of OCS. “Our goal is to help them and their families better navigate their commitment. The world isn’t getting any safer, and our freedom is not free.” AMU’s commitment to military students dates back to its start. The University was founded in 1991 by a visionary U.S. Marine Corps officer to offer career-relevant, distance education for military learners. Since then, AMU has significantly expanded this commitment – servicemembers, Reservists, spouses, legal partners, siblings and dependents can pursue bachelor's and master's degrees with preferred military tuition rates ($250 per credit hour). Visit here for more information on how to enroll at AMU . OCS offers virtual events focused on educational planning, financial literacy, and wellness support through OCS Connect for new enlisted servicemembers and their families. Recent podcasts help explain boot camp, basic training, and what to expect once enlistees are assigned to their first duty stations. AMU’s online delivery model is a hand-in-glove fit for active-duty military and their extended families – the University features asynchronous courses with monthly class starts (most are eight-week sessions). Transfer credit is possible for eligible academic coursework, job experience, and military service; AMU evaluates and applies transfer credit at no additional cost. About Our Community Salutes Our Community Salutes (OCS) is a national non-profit organization helping communities recognize, honor, and support high-school seniors who plan to enlist in the U.S. Armed Services after graduation. OCS was founded in 2009 by educator and former U.S. Army officer, Dr. Kenneth Hartman, to provide enlistees and their parents with guidance, information, resources and community support from like-minded enlistees and parents as their children start military service. OCS includes community leaders, government officials, educators, businessmen, and veterans who feel strongly in the importance of community support and recognition of the patriotic young adults who will enlist in the military after graduation. About American Public University System American Public University System (APUS) delivers affordable, high-quality, workforce-relevant higher education. With a rich, 34-year history and vibrant community of over 166,000 alumni from more than 80 countries, APUS is recognized for its innovative approach to online learning1. APUS, which includes American Military University (AMU) and American Public University (APU), is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC), an institutional accreditation agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. APUS is a wholly owned subsidiary of American Public Education, Inc. (Nasdaq: APEI). For more information, visit www.apus.edu . 1 APUS has been honored with the online Learning Consortium’s Gomory Award for Quality Online Education and is a five-time recipient of the consortium’s Effective Practice Award https://www.apus.edu/newsroom/awards/. American Public University System, American Public University, and American Military University are not affiliated with American University or the U.S. Military. Our Community Salutes Media Contact Ryan Bauman Director, Community Engagement Ryan@ocsusa.org

title: Embedded Finance: qué es y cómo está cambiando los servicios financieros
summary: El Embedded Finance integra servicios financieros dentro de plataformas no bancarias. Descubre cómo funciona, qué tipos existen y por qué empresas como Shopify, Rappi y Apple ya lo usan.
body_text: Embedded Finance: cuando los servicios financieros dejan de vivir en el banco Los servicios financieros ya no tienen que vivir en un banco. Descubre qué es el Embedded Finance, cómo funciona y por qué cada vez más empresas no financieras lo están integrando en sus plataformas. Junio 2026 por Equipo Koywe Piensa en la última vez que pediste un Uber. Tomaste el auto, llegaste a tu destino y te bajaste. No abriste una app de pagos, no sacaste una tarjeta, no firmaste nada. El cobro simplemente ocurrió. Eso es embedded finance en su forma más cotidiana: un servicio financiero tan integrado en una experiencia que casi no lo notas. El término suena técnico, pero la idea es simple: los servicios financieros (pagos, crédito, seguros, inversiones) ya no tienen que vivir exclusivamente en un banco o en una app financiera. Pueden integrarse directamente en cualquier plataforma digital, desde un marketplace hasta un software de gestión empresarial. ¿Qué significa exactamente? Embedded Finance es la integración de servicios financieros dentro de plataformas que no son bancos ni instituciones financieras tradicionales. Algunos ejemplos concretos: Shopify: ofrece préstamos a sus merchants directamente desde el dashboard donde gestionan su tienda. No necesitan ir a un banco. Amazon: permite a sus vendedores acceder a financiamiento basado en su historial de ventas en la plataforma. Apple Pay: convierte cualquier iPhone en un terminal de pago sin necesidad de hardware adicional. Rappi: en Latinoamérica ofrece una cuenta digital y tarjeta de crédito a sus usuarios dentro de la misma app donde piden comida. El denominador común: el servicio financiero está donde ya está el usuario, integrado en su flujo natural de trabajo o consumo, sin redirecciones a otro sitio ni formularios adicionales. ¿Por qué esto es posible ahora y no antes? La respuesta corta: las APIs y el modelo de Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS). Históricamente, ofrecer servicios financieros requería una licencia bancaria, infraestructura regulatoria compleja y años de construcción. Eso significaba que solo los bancos podían ser bancos. Lo que cambió es que hoy existen proveedores especializados que abstraen toda esa complejidad en interfaces de programación (APIs) que cualquier empresa puede consumir. Una startup de e-commerce no necesita convertirse en banco para ofrecer crédito a sus compradores: puede conectarse a un proveedor que ya tiene la infraestructura y la regulación resuelta, y ofrecer ese servicio como si fuera propio. Es el mismo principio que permitió que cualquier empresa ofrezca mapas sin construir su propio sistema de GPS (usan Google Maps API) o almacenamiento sin tener sus propios servidores (usan AWS). La infraestructura se volvió accesible vía API, y los servicios financieros no fueron la excepción. Los números detrás del fenómeno El Embedded Finance no es una tendencia emergente. Ya es un mercado con dimensiones concretas. El mercado global de Embedded Finance fue valorado en $108.55 mil millones en 2024 y se proyecta que alcance $1.2 billones para 2033, con una tasa de crecimiento compuesta del 28.5%, según IMARC Group. El Foro Económico Mundial estima que el mercado podría alcanzar $7.2 billones para 2030. $108.55 mil millones en 2024 Según IMARC El segmento que lidera hoy es el de pagos integrados: los embedded payments representan el 29.2% del mercado en 2024, impulsados por su adopción en e-commerce, ride-sharing, delivery de alimentos y plataformas de suscripción. ¿Qué tipos de servicios se pueden embeber? El concepto abarca mucho más que pagos: Pagos integrados. El caso más común y maduro. El pago ocurre dentro de la plataforma sin salir de ella. Uber, Airbnb, cualquier e-commerce con checkout fluido. Crédito integrado. Más conocido como Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL). Klarna, Afterpay, y en Latam empresas como Kueski ofrecen financiamiento en el momento de la compra, sin que el usuario tenga que ir a un banco. Seguros integrados. Cuando compras un vuelo y te ofrecen seguro de viaje en el mismo checkout, eso es embedded insurance. Tesla lo hace al vender autos con seguro incluido en la compra. Cuentas y tarjetas. Empresas no financieras que ofrecen cuentas digitales o tarjetas de crédito a sus usuarios. Rappi, Mercado Libre con Mercado Pago, o el caso de Apple Card. Inversiones. Plataformas que permiten invertir dinero sin salir de la app. Algunas fintech de nómina permiten que empleados invierten una fracción de su salario directamente desde la misma app donde lo reciben. ¿Por qué les importa a las empresas no financieras? Hay dos razones principales: ingresos y retención. Ingresos nuevos: Cada vez que un usuario paga, financia o asegura algo dentro de tu plataforma, la empresa recibe una comisión o margen. Para plataformas con mucho volumen de transacciones, eso puede convertirse en una línea de ingresos significativa. Retención y engagement: Los usuarios que tienen sus finanzas dentro de una plataforma tienden a usarla más y a irse menos. Es mucho más difícil dejar una app donde tienes tu cuenta, tu historial de crédito y tus pagos automáticos que una donde solo compras de vez en cuando. Shopify es quizás el caso más citado: sus servicios financieros (Shopify Payments, Shopify Capital, Shopify Balance) generan hoy una proporción creciente de sus ingresos totales, y son un factor clave en la retención de sus merchants. ¿Y para empresas B2B? Embedded Finance no es solo para consumidores. En el mundo B2B, la integración de servicios financieros en software empresarial está creciendo rápidamente. Un ERP que ofrece financiamiento de cuentas por cobrar directamente en la interfaz donde ya gestionas tus facturas. Un software de nómina que permite a los empleados acceder a adelantos de salario sin pasar por recursos humanos. Una plataforma de logística que ofrece seguro de carga al momento de crear un envío. En todos estos casos, el servicio financiero aparece en el contexto exacto donde es relevante, no en una app separada que el usuario tiene que recordar abrir. El futuro cercano Lo que estamos viendo es apenas el comienzo. La infraestructura de APIs financieras se está volviendo más accesible, la regulación en muchos mercados está avanzando hacia marcos que facilitan este tipo de integración (Open Banking en Europa y Latinoamérica, por ejemplo), y la expectativa de los usuarios, tanto consumidores como empresas, es cada vez más que los servicios financieros estén donde los necesitan, no donde históricamente han vivido. La pregunta para cualquier empresa digital ya no es si debería considerar integrar servicios financieros. Es cuándo y cómo hacerlo de forma que agregue valor real a sus usuarios. title: What is the difference between bulk and single cell RNA sequencing?
summary: This blog compares bulk vs. single cell RNA-seq. How does each technology work? What is an average gene expression readout, and what is a single cell readout?
body_text: How do you understand a biological sample? Among many other features to explore, gene expression can reveal the composition and quality of a sample by focusing on its cellular makeup. Two approaches to detect gene expression levels from cells in a complex biological sample dominate the research world: bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) and single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Before you can weigh their strengths, you need to know what each one actually does. What is bulk RNA-seq? Bulk RNA-seq is a next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based method to measure the whole transcriptome across a population of cells. Bulk pools every cell together and hands you one profile for the whole sample as an average. That means you get average expression levels for individual genes across all cells that compose the sample. Steps in a bulk experiment You start a bulk experiment by digesting your sample to extract its RNA. That could be total RNA from the sample, or you can enrich mRNA or deplete ribosomal RNA. Then you convert the RNA into cDNA and follow more processing steps to prepare a sequencing-ready gene expression library. After sequencing and data analysis, you can review gene expression levels across the tissue sample. This video provides an overview of several common methods to measure gene expression, and gets you ready to go deeper into the differences between bulk RNA-seq and single cell RNA-seq: What is single cell RNA-seq? (Seeing every tree vs. the forest) scRNA-seq is a method for studying the whole transcriptome gene expression profile of each individual cell from a sample. While a bulk readout is like the view of a forest, a single cell readout is like seeing every tree. As such, there are a few key experimental differences. Sample preparation for single cell RNA-seq scRNA-seq measurements come from individual cells, as opposed to a pool of cells. First, you need to generate viable single cell suspensions from whole samples that you digest through an enzymatic or mechanical process, cell sorting, or other cell isolation technique. Then you perform cell counting and quality control steps to ensure your samples have an appropriate concentration of viable cells and are free of clumps and cell debris. You can also stain your sample with antibodies to label proteins and other biological analytes, or perform FACS enrichment for cell types of interest. These steps for dissociating your sample will vary based on your starting material and your experimental goals. Additional preparation steps may be necessary depending on the quality of the tissue, sample abundance, cell size, or if you need to extract nuclei for chromatin accessibility profiling. Regardless of these specific considerations, the same basic principle of generating a high-quality single cell suspension applies across sample types. Instrument-enabled cell partitioning Single cell RNA-seq, like bulk RNA-seq, seeks to isolate RNA and convert it to cDNA, enabling measurement of gene expression across the whole transcriptome through next-generation sequencing. Because every readout traces back to its cell of origin, you can use the same workflow to capture more than RNA—protein, chromatin, and even immune receptor sequences, all from the same cell. In the 10x Genomics scRNA-seq workflow, you isolate single cells into individual micro-reaction vessels (Gel Beads-in-emulsion, or GEMs) before isolating RNA. This partitioning step happens in an automated, controlled environment within a microfluidic chip loaded onto a Chromium X series instrument. Then, within the GEM, Gel Beads get dissolved, releasing oligos containing unique barcodes. The cell is also lysed in order to capture the RNA molecules, which are barcoded with cell-specific barcodes. This ensures analytes from each cell can be traced back to their cell of origin. Those barcoded products are then used to create a sequencing library, allowing measurement of gene expression across the entire transcriptome of each individual cell. Figure 1. An illustration of cells or nuclei moving through a microfluidic channel and generating GEMs within a Chromium X series instrument. These are the essential steps of a single cell workflow, and the end result is a sequencing-ready gene expression library. A beginner’s guide to single cell RNA-seq Want more helpful resources to learn about single cell RNA-seq? Explore what it can do, advantages over other methods, available products, and common barriers to using the technology in our learning hub. Start here

body_text: All of the amounts disclosed in this press release are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise noted TEL AVIV, Israel, Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enlight Renewable Energy (NASDAQ: ENLT, TASE: ENLT) today reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Registration links for the Company’s earnings English and Hebrew conference call and webcasts can be found at the end of this earnings release. The entire suite of the Company’s 2 Q2 6 financial results can be found on our IR website at https://enlightenergy.com/data/financial-reports/ Financial Highlights 3 months ending June 30, 202 6 Total revenues and income1 of $210 million, an increase of 55% compared to the same period last year. Net income of $31 million, compared to $6 million in the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA2 of $160 million, compared to $96 million in the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA of $314 million, compared to $227 million in the first half of 2025. Our first-half results, together with the continued advancement of projects under construction and the expansion of our energy storage business, enable us to raise our 2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance, as well as the run-rate revenues reflected in our mature projects and our year-end 2028 target. At the same time, the successful completion of $2.6 billion financing for the CO Bar complex, the largest in our history, along with additional milestones achieved during the quarter, highlights Enlight’s execution and financing capabilities and reflects the confidence of our financial partners. We remain focused and disciplined in expanding our global portfolio and converting it into sustained high-growth performance while preserving long-term profitability. At the same time, we continue to strengthen our position as a leading energy platform across the markets in which we operate.” Portfolio R eview During the second quarter and through the date of this release, Enlight continued to expand its portfolio and advance projects through the various phases of development. As of the earning release date, Enlight’s total portfolio is comprised of 21.8 GW of generation capacity and 74.6 GWh energy storage (totaling 43.1 FGW5), representing an increase of 4.6 % compared to the total portfolio at the release date of the first quarter of 2026 (41.2 FGW). The generation component increased by approximately 1.5% and the storage component increased by approximately 8 % compared to the previous quarter, reflecting Enlight’s strategy to lead in energy storage as a response to the market’s increasing demand. The mature component of the portfolio (operating projects, projects under construction, and projects in pre-construction) comprises of 6.4 GW of generation capacity and 20.5 GWh of storage capacity, totaling 12.3 FGW, compared to 11.6 FGW at the end of the previous quarter, an increase of 6%. Approximately 53% of the capacity is located in the U.S., 32% in Europe, and approximately 15% in MENA. The advanced development and development components comprise of 15.4 GW of generation capacity and 54.1 GWh of storage capacity, totaling 30.8 FGW, an increase of 4% sequentially. Non-IFRS Financial Measures This release presents Adjusted EBITDA, a non-IFRS financial metric, which is provided as a complement to the results provided in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (“IFRS”). A reconciliation of the non-IFRS financial information to the most directly comparable IFRS financial measure is provided in the accompanying tables found at the end of this release. We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) plus depreciation and amortization, share based compensation, finance expenses, taxes on income and share in losses of equity accounted investees, minus finance income and adjusted to eliminate any non-recurring portions of other income (expenses), net. compensation received in respect of contractual performance shortfalls and recorded in other income (expenses), net, is included in adjusted EBITDA. Such compensation represents income the company would have generated had the contractual performance levels been achieved. With respect to gains (losses) from asset disposals, as part of Enlight’s strategy to accelerate growth and reduce the need for equity financing, the Company sells parts of or the entirety of selected renewable project assets from time to time, and therefore includes realized gains or losses from these asset disposals in Adjusted EBITDA. In the case of partial assets disposals, Adjusted EBITDA includes only the economic gain or loss attributable to the interest sold, calculated as the consideration received less the proportional book value attributable to such interest. Our management believes Adjusted EBITDA is indicative of operational performance and ongoing profitability and uses Adjusted EBITDA to evaluate the operating performance and for planning and forecasting purposes. Non-IFRS financial measures have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation or as substitutes for financial information presented under IFRS. There are a number of limitations related to the use of non-IFRS financial measures versus comparable financial measures determined under IFRS. Investors are encouraged to review the related IFRS financial measure, Net Income, and the reconciliations of Adjusted EBITDA provided below to Net Income and to not rely on any single financial measure to evaluate our business. About Enlight Founded in 2008, Enlight develops, finances, constructs, owns, and operates utility-scale renewable energy projects. Enlight has been traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange since 2010 (TASE: ENLT) and completed its U.S. IPO (Nasdaq: ENLT) in 2023. Net financial debt to EBITDA So long as debentures F remain outstanding, standalone financial debt shall not exceed NIS 10 million, and the consolidated financial debt to EBITDA ratio shall not exceed 18 for more than two consecutive financial periods. Equity to balance sheet The standalone equity to total balance sheet ratio shall be maintained at no less than 20% ,25% and 28%, respectively, for two consecutive financial periods for as long as debentures F, debentures C and D and debentures G and H remain outstanding. Appendix 4 – Change in accounting policy Until September 30, 2025, interest paid and interest received were presented within cash flows from operating activities in the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows. In accordance with IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows , entities are permitted to classify interest paid and interest received as operating, investing, or financing cash flows, provided that the selected classification is applied consistently from period to period. During the fourth quarter of 2025, management elected to change the classification of interest paid, including payments relating to interest rate swap (IRS) instruments to cash flows used in financing activities, and interest received to cash flows from investing activities. title: Bread Financial® creates meaningful community impact through partnerships, volunteering
summary: Making smart, well-informed decisions is the key to financial freedom. We hope these great tips will enhance your shopping experiences.
body_text: Back to People & Culture Culture August 17, 2026 Bread Financial® creates meaningful community impact through partnerships, volunteering Bread Financial® ' s recent community efforts show that small actions, multiplied across the organization, create meaningful change. Over the past three months, Bread Financial gave $1.87 million in grants to nonprofits, 758 associates volunteered with 138 different charities , and more than $470,000 was donated through associate donations and company matching gifts. During Pay It Forward Week in May, associates contributed more than 1,000 volunteer hours with 34 charities . The company also helped provide an estimated 1.98 million meals for families in need through Operation Feed, its fundraising campaign to support hunger relief globally. Read below to see how Bread Financial and its associates continue to show up for the community. Campaign spotlight: Taking steps for kids' mental health In May 2026, Bread Financial partnered with The Kids Mental Health Foundation (KMHF ) , the leading organization advancing children’s mental health in the United States, on several initiatives during Mental Health Awareness Month. The month began with a $300,000 gift to help expand access to trusted tools and practical guidance so parents, caregivers and other adults have what they need to support kids through stress, change and everyday challenges. Throughout the month, Bread Financial and KMHF recognized Kids Mental Health Day at The Grove in Los Angeles, hosted a webinar for Bread Financial associates on kids' mental health and technology, and helped launch a new curriculum for educators to better support military-connected students. The company closed the month by serving as the presenting sponsor of the 2026 5K for Kids' Mental Health, held at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in Columbus, Ohio. Hosted by the Columbus Crew , the event brought together nearly 1,400 runners, walkers, volunteers and supporters from across almost 20 states, united by the belief that every child deserves the mental health support they need to thrive. Bread Financial’s 52-member team not only joined the race, but raised nearly $2,000 as the top fundraising team. Together, participants and sponsors raised more than $250,000. Image Bread Financial associates pictured at the 2026 5K for Kids' Mental Health Volunteer spotlight: Creative giving and meals for students During Operation Feed, nearly 80 India associates volunteered their creativity and time to help design and create tote bags supported through Akshaya Patra , a non-governmental organization, dedicated to providing nutritious meals to school children. Later in the month, 40 associates helped serve meals at Government High School in Bettahalasur, India. Together, they served meals to 250 students and distributed the tote bags. Through Operation Feed, Bread Financial supported 480 students in India with midday meals for an entire year, extending the impact of associate volunteerism beyond a single day of service. Image Bread Financial India associates posing with their finished tote bags. Grant spotlight: Growing girls’ confidence In the first half of 2026, Bread Financial awarded grants to 19 nonprofits, reflecting the company's commitment to its value, "Be kind and pay it forward." Each organization’s mission aligns with Bread Financial’s purpose-driven priorities: fostering thriving communities, advancing financial wellness and protecting our planet. Bread Financial also renewed its partnership with Ruling Our eXperiences (ROX) , the national authority on research, education and programming for girls, with a $1.8 million grant. With this support, ROX plans to expand access to its programs, release an updated edition of The Girls' Index™ in 2028 alongside additional research briefs, and host its largest annual fundraiser, Girls Without Limits. The grant builds on a long-standing partnership between ROX and Bread Financial. In 2025, with the company's backing, ROX reached all 50 states through its "Fast to 50" initiative. With sustained funding and a nationwide presence, ROX can continue supporting thousands of girls each year. “The future of our girls – and by extension, the future of our world – depends on our willingness to listen, understand and act,” said Dr. Lisa Hinkelman , founder and CEO of ROX. “It depends on our shared commitment to invest in girls, to provide them with the support and resources they need to flourish.” Image The ROX team pictured at the 2026 Girls Without Limits fundraiser. Partner spotlight: Action for Children Action for Children (AFC) is a local childcare resource and referral agency in central Ohio, serving families and providers across Franklin, Delaware, Fairfield, Licking, Madison, Pickaway and Union counties. With more than 50 years of history in the Columbus area, AFC helps transform children’s lives by supporting the adults who care for and educate them. This year, with funding from Bread Financial, AFC completed its All Our Kin 10-Week Business Series and Coaching Program, which helps family childcare educators manage and grow their home-based businesses. The program covered topics including marketing, accounting, financial management and more. Graduates also had the opportunity to continue their journey through one-on-one business coaching. The program concluded with a graduation to celebrate and reflect on the program. “We are so proud of each graduate and inspired by the growth, dedication and vision shown throughout the series,” said Tonya Smoot , Program Manager of Action for Children. “From laughter and fellowship to the meaningful moments shared, the evening was truly one to remember. Thank you to everyone who helped make this year impactful!” About Bread Financial®​ Bread Financial® (NYSE: BFH) is a tech-forward financial services company that provides simple, personalized payment, lending and saving solutions to millions of U.S. consumers. Our payment solutions deliver growth for some of the most recognized brands in travel & entertainment, health & beauty, technology, electronics, jewelry, home and specialty apparel through our co-brand and private label credit cards and pay-over-time products providing choice and value to our shared customers. Additionally, we offer Bread Financial general purpose credit cards and saving products that empower our customers and their passions for a better life.​ Bread Financial proudly marks 30 years of success in 2026. To learn more about our global associates, our performance and our sustainability progress, visit breadfinancial.com or follow us on Instagram and LinkedIn .
